newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU raids firms in amino-acid price fixing probe.
newsitem.headline: EU raids firms in amino-acid price fixing probe.

text.p: The European Commission said on Thursday it was investigating a series of companies, including ADM Co over allegations of price-fixing in the amino acids market.
It said it was currently raiding the offices of companies in Germany and Britain in connection with the probe.

"I can confirm our inspectors have been conducting (raids) at the European headquarters of a series of companies...our inspectors are still around, apparently in Germany and the United Kingdom," an EU spokesman said.
The spokesman confirmed that ADM was being investigated as the company announced on Wednesday but declined to name the other companies.

Archer Daniels Midland Co. (ADM), which pleaded guilty to price-fixing charges in the U.S. last year, said it and several of its European subsidiaries were among the subjects of an anti-competitive practices investigation by the Commission.

The huge U.S. agricultural products processor said in a statement the Commission was probing the possible participation of major manufacturers in anticompetitive practices or agreements in certain markets for amino acids, including the feed additive lysine, in the European Union.
ADM pleaded guilty in the U.S. last year to fixing prices of lysine and the food additive citric acid, and paid a record $100 million in fines.
The U.S. Justice Department probe also resulted in charges against Ajinimoto Co Inc and Kyowa Hakko Kogyo Co Ltd of Japan and Sewon America Inc.
ADM said the Commission probe was in its early stages and the outcome could not be predicted. -- Brussels Newsroom 32 2 287 6800
